identity.title: ReGenesis: LLMs can Grow into Reasoning Generalists via Self-Improvement

problem.claim: The paper examines whether an LLM can improve reasoning by self-synthesizing reasoning paths for post-training without additional supervision.

gap.claim: Existing self-synthesizing methods reportedly generalize poorly to out-of-domain reasoning tasks, which the authors hypothesize results from task-specific paths lacking task-agnostic guidance.

contributions.claim: ReGenesis self-synthesizes post-training reasoning paths by progressing from abstract reasoning guidance to concrete task-specific paths.
The authors report that ReGenesis outperforms existing methods across all tested in-domain and out-of-domain settings, with analysis across language models and design choices.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish ReGenesis by converting general reasoning guidelines into task-specific ones, generating reasoning structures, and then transforming them into reasoning paths without human-designed task-specific examples used by existing methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance over existing methods in every tested in-domain and out-of-domain setting.
Across six out-of-domain tasks, previous methods reportedly decreased by about 4.6% on average after post-training, whereas ReGenesis improved performance by about 6.1%.
The authors report effectiveness across various language models and design choices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reasoning trajectories can improve LLM reasoning, but obtaining high-quality trajectories may require costly or license-constrained supervision.
The paper explores unsupervised self-synthesis and identifies poor out-of-domain generalization in existing methods.
The authors attribute this limitation to task-specific self-synthesized paths that lack general reasoning guidance.
ReGenesis moves from general guidelines to structures and concrete paths; the authors report gains over existing methods, including on six out-of-domain tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links out-of-domain generalization to a pipeline that moves from task-agnostic guidelines through reasoning structures to task-specific paths, and reports positive results on six out-of-domain tasks.

lessons.interpretation: Separating general reasoning guidance from task-specific realization can make a self-improvement procedure more explicitly target transfer.
lessons.application: When proposing self-generated training data, describe intermediate abstractions and test whether they support transfer beyond the source task.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target domain depends primarily on highly specialized procedures that cannot be captured by general guidance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six out-of-domain tasks, evaluation metrics, model identities, datasets, or statistical uncertainty behind the reported percentages.
The reported causal explanation for prior methods' poor generalization is presented as a hypothesis, not as independently established evidence.
The abstract does not provide implementation details sufficient to assess reproducibility or determine which design choices drive the gains.
